name: Lexical Semantic Change Detection in German (Shared Task)
description: Recent NLP architectures have illustrated in various ways how semantic change can be captured across time and domains. However, in terms of evaluation there is a lack of benchmarks to compare the performance of these systems against each other. We present the results of the first shared task on unsupervised lexical semantic change detection (LSCD) in German based on the evaluation framework proposed by Schlechtweg et al. (2019).
general_score_metric: Spearman's rank correlation (for graded/ranking) and accuracy (for binary change detection)
reputation: The first shared task for German lexical semantic change detection; respected within the semantic-change and historical linguistics NLP community but relatively niche compared to mainstream NLP benchmarks.
notes: Language-specific (German) and relatively small-scale shared-task data; includes both binary and graded change evaluations. Risk of contamination from pretrained embeddings if contemporary large pretrained models are used; not an LLM-specific benchmark.
